passage.title: Teacher-written opinion article for the Year 8 progress assessment (TGA)
paras: Every summer our town spends thousands of pounds on plastic water bottles for its festival. Every autumn, the bottles turn up in the river. There is a better way. Ten public drinking fountains would cost less than two years of bottles, and they would still be working long after the last festival flag is folded away. Some people say fountains are unhygienic. Modern fountains are cleaned daily and tested weekly. The real question is not whether we can afford fountains. It is whether we can afford to keep filling the river.

keywords.def: what a writer thinks about a topic
a text you have not studied before

questions.q: Before the timer: underline the key words in question 3
questions.a: Question 3: 'How does the writer argue against the counter-argument?': key words 'argue against' and 'counter-argument'.

questions.q: Core (timed, 20 minutes): Section A. 1) What turns up in the river every autumn? (1) 2) Give two advantages of fountains from the article. (2) 3) How does the writer deal with the counter-argument? (5) 4) How does the writer persuade the reader? Use PETZAAL. (8)
questions.a: 1) plastic bottles. 2) cheaper than two years of bottles; last long after the festival; cleaned daily and tested weekly. 3) states it ('Some people say fountains are unhygienic') then refutes it with facts (cleaned daily, tested weekly). 4) e.g. repetition 'Every summer / Every autumn', contrast of afford fountains / afford to keep filling the river, rhetorical reframing in the last line.

questions.q: Extend (timed, 8 minutes): Section B. 5) Embed 'filling the river' in an analytical sentence. (2) 6) Begin a sentence about the article with a subordinate clause. (2) 7) Expand the noun phrase 'fountains' with two modifiers. (2) 8) Correct: 'the towns festival is fun, it makes alot of waste' (2)
questions.a: 5) e.g. 'The writer's image of 'filling the river' makes waste sound deliberate.' 6) e.g. 'Although the festival is popular, it creates waste.' 7) e.g. 'ten modern public fountains'. 8) The town's festival is fun, but it makes a lot of waste.

questions.q: Stretch: if time remains, check apostrophes and sentence boundaries in every answer
Where is the writer's viewpoint clearest?
questions.a: B) the final two sentences. The ending states the real question and the writer's answer.
